evidenceBoundary: Static code inspection and deterministic scripted-provider tests only. No live cloud inference was invoked.

problemRecovered.runtime: The production planner accepted only the legacy tasks/assignedRole graph.
problemRecovered.qualification: The previous qualification probe accepted a looser task shape that did not match production's required summary and fields.
problemRecovered.risk: A model could be marked planner-capable under qualification yet be rejected by runtime solely for wire-format incompatibility.

change.legacyProtocol: task_graph_v1 remains accepted, including payloads that predate the explicit protocol field.
change.semanticProtocol: semantic_steps_v1 accepts explicit id, intent, phase, and after fields and canonicalizes phases to the same explorer/planner/coder/reviewer graph.
safety: A semantic payload may not mix legacy task-graph fields.
Unknown phases and missing dependency lists fail closed.
Canonical output still passes planning completeness, graph authorization, dependency validation, review, ForgeVerify, and the completion gate.
change.qualificationVersion: PLANNER_PROTOCOL_V2 under R27_ROLE_QUALIFICATION_V2; PLANNER_PROTOCOL_V1 remains retained for historical receipt interpretation.

proven: Both explicit task-graph and semantic-steps payloads are parsed to one canonical PlannerResult.
Malformed, mixed, unknown-phase, and dependency-incomplete semantic payloads are rejected before authorization.
The production Explorer-to-Planner-to-Coder-to-Reviewer pipeline completes with a semantic planner payload only after existing verification and completion checks pass.
Planner qualification now uses the production parser instead of a looser duplicate schema.
notProven: Live improvement in planner qualification rate.
Live token, latency, or completion-rate benefit.
A live crossover threshold for choosing semantic_steps_v1.
requiredNextEvidence: Run paired live, free-route planner tasks with the same repository state, budget, verifier, and completion criteria. Record provider receipts and preserve route, quota, or availability failures as blockers.
